topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture within the cancer course and states its learning objectives.

topics.label: Cancer evolution and the origins of susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how mutations arising in susceptible cells can support clonal evolution into cancer within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risk: chance, exposure and population evidence
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics weigh evidence for environmental contributions to cancer against explanations based on chance or inherited susceptibility.

topics.label: Infectious causes of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infections can contribute to carcinogenesis, with Burkitt lymphoma illustrating the interaction between pathogens and tumour development.

topics.label: Mechanisms of DNA damage from environmental carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how environmental exposures produce DNA damage and mutations through processes shaped by cellular metabolism and repair.

topics.label: Tumour initiation and promotion
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show why mutational initiation may require subsequent promotion that enables altered cells to proliferate.

topics.label: Biological context and carcinogen susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological circumstances influence carcinogenic effects and consolidate that dependence within the lecture's account of cancer causation.

topics.label: Inferring carcinogen exposure from mutational signatures
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how characteristic mutation patterns in cancer genomes can provide evidence of previous carcinogen exposure.

topics.label: Assessing carcinogenicity and the limitations of testing
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how carcinogenic potential can be investigated when available methods cannot fully reproduce human exposure and tumour development.

topics.label: Closing summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by summarising its conclusions in terms of everyday risk–benefit decisions.
